entries.name: Didit AML Screening
entries.description: Screen a person or company name against global sanctions, PEP, watchlist, and adverse-media datasets. Returns a hit list with per-hit match/risk scores and an overall review status.

usage.callShape: POST JSON {full_name} (single string; optional entity_type 'person'|'company' default person, date_of_birth YYYY-MM-DD, nationality ISO-3166-1 alpha-2 e.g. 'ES', document_number, include_adverse_media bool ~+10s, tuning weights aml_name_weight/aml_dob_weight/aml_country_weight must sum to 100). x402 exact, $0.36 USDC on Base.
usage.outputShape: request_id; aml.status ('In Review'|...); aml.total_hits; aml.entity_type; aml.hits[] each {id,url,match(bool),score,caption,datasets[],risk_score,match_score,review_status('Unreviewed'),risk_view{crimes,countries,categories},properties{name[],alias[],birthDate[],address[],gender[]},score_breakdown{name_score,dob_score,...}}
quirks: Required field is full_name (single string), NOT first_name/last_name — wrong shape 400s with {full_name:[This field is required.]}.
DISTINCT from /v3/database-validation — this screens a name against sanctions/PEP/adverse-media; it does NOT validate a real ID against a national registry.
Response is huge for common names (~476KB / 86 hits for 'John Smith'). Filter aml.hits[] by .match==true or high .match_score/.risk_score rather than dumping the array.
Many hits -> aml.status='In Review' (NOT an error); per-hit review_status defaults to 'Unreviewed'. Read aml.total_hits + inspect hits[].match_score.
nationality here is ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 (e.g. 'ES'), unlike database-validation which uses alpha-3.

entries.name: Didit Database Validation
entries.description: Validate user-provided identity data (ID number / name / DOB) against authoritative national registries. Currently supports LATAM countries + Spain only. Returns match_type and per-source validation outcomes.

usage.callShape: POST JSON, REQUIRED: issuing_state (ISO 3166-1 alpha-3, ONLY ARG/BOL/BRA/CHL/COL/CRI/DOM/ECU/ESP/GTM/HND/MEX/PAN/PER/PRY/SLV/URY/VEN), validation_type ('one_by_one'|'two_by_two'), identification_number (universal field, auto-maps to country format). Optional: document_type (P/DL/ID/RP), first_name, last_name, date_of_birth YYYY-MM-DD, nationality (alpha-3), expiration_date (required for some e.g. ESP), address. x402 exact, $0.31 USDC on Base.
usage.outputShape: request_id; database_validation.status ('Declined'|...); database_validation.issuing_state; database_validation.validation_type; database_validation.match_type ('no_match'|...); database_validation.screened_data{personal_number}; database_validation.validations[] each {service_id,service_name,validation,outcome_code,outcome_detail,source_data}; database_validation.warnings[] each {feature,risk,log_type,short_description,long_description}; created_at; vendor_data; metadata
quirks: Geographically restricted: issuing_state MUST be one of the 18 supported codes (LATAM + ESP). No US/EU-wide coverage.
issuing_state and nationality use ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 (e.g. MEX/ESP), unlike the AML endpoint which uses alpha-2.
A 200 with status 'Declined' / match_type 'no_match' is a normal NEGATIVE result (charged in full), not an error — read database_validation.match_type + validations[].outcome_code.

Some countries require extra fields (e.g. ESP needs expiration_date; document_type required for some). identification_number is a universal field that auto-maps to the country-specific format (e.g. MEX CURP).
DISTINCT from /v3/aml: this checks a real ID against a national database (e.g. mex_curp), not a sanctions/watchlist name screen.

entries.name: Identity Verification / KYC
entries.description: Verify a person's identity / run a KYC check.

usage.callShape: POST https://kyc.madhousewallet.com/api/public/kyc/start with an empty JSON body {} (Content-Type: application/json). x402 payment ($0.05 USDC on Base/Polygon/Arbitrum) is required; the paying wallet is auto-bound to the session.
usage.outputShape: body.kycUrl (hosted browser verification URL), body.walletAddress (lowercase wallet bound from x402 payment header)
quirks: inputSchema is empty — send an empty JSON body {}; no input fields are accepted or needed
walletAddress in the response is auto-extracted from the x402 payment header (lowercased) and bound to this KYC session; you do not pass it
Response is NOT a verification verdict. It returns a hosted kycUrl that a HUMAN must open in a browser to complete document + selfie verification
An EAS or SAS attestation is written automatically once a human completes the hosted flow — the API call itself does not return pass/fail
Sync response (no async job/polling on this call), but actual KYC completion is out-of-band via the browser flow
usage.guide: POST to https://kyc.madhousewallet.com/api/public/kyc/start with an empty JSON body {}. It costs $0.05 USDC via x402 (Base, Polygon, or Arbitrum). The synchronous response gives you body.kycUrl and body.walletAddress; the walletAddress is the paying wallet, auto-bound to the session. Open body.kycUrl in a browser — a real person must complete document + selfie verification there. Once completed, an on-chain attestation (EAS/SAS) is written automatically for the bound wallet; this start call does not itself return a pass/fail result.

entries.name: Verifik
entries.description: x402-native KYC/identity verification — document liveness/authenticity, face liveness detection, live face comparison (selfie↔ID), face validation, and document validation against official registries (strong Latin-American coverage). Pay-per-check x402 on Base.

usage.callShape: POST https://ai.verifik.co/api/face-recognition/face-validation with JSON body {image} where image is a base64-encoded JPEG/PNG (data:image/jpeg;base64,... data-URI accepted)

inputExample.image: data:image/jpeg;base64,/9j/4AAQSkZJRg...<base64 of a JPEG containing a human face>

usage.outputShape: body.data (Verifik face-detection result: bounding boxes + face quality signals) and body.signature — per the 402 bazaar output schema (untested; payment never completed)
quirks: 402 accepts entries are MALFORMED for x402 USDC: the Base USDC entry (eip155:8453, asset 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913) provides extra:{name:USDC,decimals:6} but OMITS the EIP-712 domain 'version' field. Sponge requires both name AND version to build the USDC transferWithAuthorization payload, so it aborts BEFORE sending any payment (error: 'EIP-712 domain parameters (name, version) are required'). No funds were spent across 2 attempts.

Endpoint defaults to Avalanche C-Chain (eip155:43114) for payment; also offers native AVAX/ETH and Base USDC. None of the accepts entries carry an EIP-712 'version', so all USDC paths are un-payable via Sponge as-is.

Alternative documented payment flow exists: pay on-chain manually then retry with header X-PAYMENT-TX=<txHash> (or Authorization: L402 <txHash>), or bypass with a Verifik user Bearer JWT — but neither is supported by the standard qa-pay/Sponge x402 flow.
Input schema is well-defined and simple: body {image} (base64). The endpoint itself is likely functional; only the payment-requirements 402 is broken for our stack.
usage.guide: Call POST https://ai.verifik.co/api/face-recognition/face-validation with JSON {"image": "<base64 JPEG of a human face>"} (a data:image/jpeg;base64,... URI works). Expect the face-detection result under body.data plus body.signature. WARNING: as of this test the endpoint cannot be paid via the standard x402 USDC flow — its 402 'accepts' entries omit the EIP-712 domain 'version' field, so the Sponge payment provider fails to build the payload and never sends funds. To use it you would need an alternate path (manual on-chain pay + X-PAYMENT-TX header, or a Verifik user Bearer JWT), neither of which qa-pay supports.

entries.name: Greeneris EU Company Check
entries.description: One-call KYB verification of a European company across nine national registries (FR, UK, IE, NO, FI, SK, PL, CZ, CH): official registry existence and status, insolvency signals, VAT (VIES), LEI (GLEIF), sanctions screening (EU/OFAC/UN/UK/FR), EORI and optional domain age, condensed into a pass/review/fail verdict with per-check source, timestamp and an explicit coverage map.

queryParams.country: REQUIRED. Registry to check against; one of FR, UK, IE, NO, FI, SK, PL, CZ, CH
queryParams.id: REQUIRED. National registry id: SIREN/SIRET (FR), company number (UK/IE), orgnr (NO), y-tunnus (FI), ICO (SK/CZ), NIP (PL), UID CHE-... (CH)
queryParams.vat: OPTIONAL. VAT number to check when not derivable (IE, SK)
queryParams.eori: OPTIONAL. EORI customs number to validate
queryParams.domain: OPTIONAL. Company website domain for age and MX signals
queryParams.legal_entities_only: OPTIONAL boolean (default true); false = include minimized facts for individual entrepreneurs

checks.registry: object { status, exists, company_status, registered_on, source }
checks.vat: object { status, is_valid, number, name, source }
checks.lei: object { status, has_lei, lei, entity_status, jurisdiction, source }
checks.sanctions: object { status, screened_name, verdict, match_count, matches[], lists_as_of }

usage.callShape: GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/eu/company-check?country=<FR|UK|IE|NO|FI|SK|PL|CZ|CH>&id=<national_registry_id> (optional: vat, lei, eori, domain, legal_entities_only). x402 paid endpoint (~0.10 USDC on Base, no API key) — pay the 402 quote and re-request.
usage.outputShape: JSON: { ok: true, data: { subject{country,id,legal_name,natural_person}, verdict (pass|review|fail), confidence, reasons[], checks{registry,insolvency,vat,lei,sanctions,eori,domain}, coverage{checked[],not_covered[],never_covered[],degraded[]}, flags[], disclaimer, source } }. Each check carries its own status/source/timestamp.
quirks: country and id are BOTH required query params; country must be one of the 9 supported ISO codes (FR, UK, IE, NO, FI, SK, PL, CZ, CH) or the call fails.
Static price ($0.10), not a dynamic quote (amount 100000 = 0.10 USDC, 6 decimals).
Provider states buyers are NEVER charged on a failed verification (only successful pass/review/fail verdicts are billed).

Factual verification of official public records only — explicitly NOT a credit rating/score/probability-of-default. Sanctions matches are a screening aid that require human review before any business decision.

Coverage varies by country: some checks land in coverage.not_covered / degraded (e.g. UBO is never_covered EU-wide since the CJEU Nov-2022 ruling); read the coverage map, don't assume every check ran.
Optional vat/lei/eori/domain params refine or extend the checks (e.g. domain adds age + MX signals; vat needed for IE/SK where it isn't derivable).
Responses are per-check cached (registry/vat/lei ~24h, insolvency ~30min) per the cache_ttl_s fields.
Part of Greeneris 'eu-verify' — sibling ops (per-country /v1/*/company lookups, /v1/screen/sanctions, /v1/fr/supplier-risk, /v1/global/lei, /v1/validate/*) live on the same host as separate services.
usage.guide: Run one-shot KYB / due-diligence on a European company. GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/eu/company-check?country=<code>&id=<national_registry_id> where country is one of FR, UK, IE, NO, FI, SK, PL, CZ, CH and id is that country's registry number (e.g. SIREN 552032534 for FR/DANONE). Optionally add vat, lei, eori or domain to refine. It is an x402 paid endpoint (~0.10 USDC on Base, no API key) — pay the 402 quote and re-request. Read data.verdict (pass|review|fail) plus data.checks.* for the per-registry evidence and data.coverage for what was actually checked. Treat sanctions hits as review-required, not a decision.

entries.name: Greeneris French Supplier Risk
entries.description: One-call due diligence on a single French company by SIREN or SIRET: identifier checksum, existence and status (SIRENE), insolvency proceedings (BODACC), VAT validity (VIES) and sanctions screening across EU/OFAC/UN/UK/FR lists, condensed into a low/medium/high/critical risk verdict with a 0-100 score and human-readable reasons.

queryParams.siret: 14-digit French SIRET (SIREN is derived from it; provide siren OR siret)

data.company: object { exists, active, legal_name, naf, creation_date }
data.sanctions: object { status, screened_name, verdict, match_count, matches[] }
data.source: string (SIRENE + BODACC + VIES + sanctions index provenance)

usage.callShape: GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/fr/supplier-risk?siren=<9-digit SIREN> (or ?siret=<14-digit SIRET>). x402 paid endpoint (0.05 USDC on Base, no API key) — pay the 402 quote and re-request.
usage.outputShape: JSON: { ok: true, data: { siren, identifier_valid, company{exists,active,legal_name,naf,creation_date}, vat{number,status}, insolvency{status,records_found,latest}, sanctions{status,screened_name,verdict,match_count,matches[]}, risk{level(low|medium|high|critical),score(0-100),reasons[]}, source } }.
quirks: Provide exactly one of siren (9 digits) or siret (14 digits) as a query param; siren is derived from siret when siret is given.
Static price ($0.05), not a dynamic quote (amount 50000 = 0.05 USDC, 6 decimals).
Provider states buyers are NEVER charged on failure; sub-checks degrade gracefully (a partial answer still returns rather than erroring).
France-only. For multi-country KYB use the sibling Greeneris EU Company Check (/v1/eu/company-check); for a plain FR registry lookup use /v1/fr/company.

The risk verdict/score is a screening aid built from official public records (SIRENE/BODACC/VIES + EU/OFAC/UN/UK/FR sanctions), NOT a credit rating or probability-of-default; sanctions hits require human review.
Part of Greeneris 'eu-verify' — sibling ops (/v1/eu/company-check, /v1/screen/sanctions, per-country /v1/*/company, /v1/fr/bodacc, /v1/validate/*) live on the same host as separate services.
usage.guide: Run one-shot due diligence / supplier risk on a French company. GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/fr/supplier-risk?siren=<9-digit SIREN> (e.g. 552032534 for DANONE) or ?siret=<14-digit SIRET>. It is an x402 paid endpoint (0.05 USDC on Base, no API key) — pay the 402 quote and re-request. Read data.risk.level (low|medium|high|critical) and data.risk.score (0-100) for the verdict, plus data.company / data.vat / data.insolvency / data.sanctions for the underlying evidence. Treat sanctions matches as review-required, not an automatic decision.

entries.name: Greeneris Sanctions Screening
entries.description: Screen a person or company name against the five official sanctions lists (EU, US OFAC SDN, UN, UK FCDO, French asset freezes) from a daily-refreshed snapshot, returning scored fuzzy matches with entity type and programs plus a match / possible_match / no_match verdict.

queryParams.name: REQUIRED. Person or company name to screen (2-120 chars)
queryParams.threshold: OPTIONAL. Fuzzy match threshold 0.6-1.0 as decimal (default 0.85)
queryParams.lists: OPTIONAL. Comma-separated subset of eu,ofac,un,uk,fr (default: all)

data.matches: object[] { list, list_label, entity_id, entity_type, primary_name, matched_name, programs, score }

usage.callShape: GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/screen/sanctions?name=<person or company name> (optional: threshold=0.6-1.0, lists=eu,ofac,un,uk,fr). x402 paid endpoint (~0.01 USDC on Base, no API key) — pay the 402 quote and re-request.
usage.outputShape: JSON: { ok: true, data: { query, threshold, verdict (match|possible_match|no_match), match_count, matches[]{list,list_label,entity_id,entity_type,primary_name,matched_name,programs,score}, lists_checked{eu,fr,ofac,uk,un: {entities,names,as_of}}, lists_unavailable[], disclaimer, source } }.
quirks: name is the only required query param; 2-120 chars.
Static price ($0.01), not a dynamic quote (amount 10000 = 0.01 USDC, 6 decimals).

verdict is one of match | possible_match | no_match; score is string-similarity (0-1), NOT identity verification — a 'match' requires human review (date of birth, nationality) before any business decision per the provider disclaimer.
Optional threshold (default 0.85) tunes fuzzy sensitivity; optional lists narrows which of the five lists (eu,ofac,un,uk,fr) are screened (default: all).
lists_checked reports the per-list entity/name counts and as_of dates of the snapshot; snapshot is refreshed daily.
Part of Greeneris 'eu-verify' — sibling ops (/v1/eu/company-check, per-country /v1/*/company lookups, /v1/global/lei, /v1/validate/*) live on the same host as separate services.
usage.guide: Screen a name against the five official sanctions lists (EU, US OFAC SDN, UN, UK FCDO, FR asset freezes). GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/screen/sanctions?name=<person or company name>; optionally pass threshold (0.6-1.0, default 0.85) and lists (comma-separated subset of eu,ofac,un,uk,fr, default all). It is an x402 paid endpoint (~0.01 USDC on Base, no API key) — pay the 402 quote and re-request. Read data.verdict (match|possible_match|no_match) and data.matches[] (list, primary_name, programs, score) for hits, and data.lists_checked for the snapshot dates. Treat any match as review-required, not a decision.

entries.name: Greeneris LEI Validation
entries.description: Offline Legal Entity Identifier (LEI) validation: ISO 17442 structure regex plus ISO 7064 mod 97-10 checksum over the 20-char code, returning valid, LOU prefix, entity part and check digits (no GLEIF registry lookup).

inputSchema.lei: string (required, 20 characters) — LEI to validate, passed as the ?lei= query param

data.lou_prefix: string (first 4 chars — Local Operating Unit prefix)
data.source: string (validation method description); a failure reason is returned when valid is false

usage.callShape: GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/validate/lei?lei=<20-char LEI>. No request body. Synchronous JSON response. Pay via x402 exact, $0.002 USDC on Base (eip155:8453).
usage.outputShape: body.ok (bool); body.data{ lei, valid (bool), lou_prefix (4-char LOU), entity_part (14-char), check_digits (2-char), source }. When the code is malformed/fails checksum, body.data.valid is false with a failure reason.
quirks: Pure OFFLINE computation (structure regex + ISO 7064 mod 97-10 checksum) — it does NOT hit the GLEIF registry, so it confirms a LEI is well-formed, not that the entity exists. For the live GLEIF record use the sibling /v1/global/lei; for the ownership tree use /v1/lei/ownership.

DISTINCT operation from /v1/validate/iban, /v1/validate/isin, /v1/validate/bic, /v1/validate/email — each sibling takes its own query param and returns its own schema (not path-param variants of one op).
1-year cache; read-only, not outward/irreversible.
Paid GET returned confirmed:false (no txHash echoed) but HTTP 200 with the full body — settlement confirmation is async/not echoed; the 200 body is the proof of success.
usage.guide: Validate a Legal Entity Identifier (LEI) offline before regulatory reporting (EMIR/MiFID II require a valid LEI per counterparty) or before hitting the GLEIF registry — ISO 17442 structure regex plus ISO 7064 mod 97-10 checksum over the 20-char code. GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/validate/lei?lei=<20-char LEI> with no body; synchronous JSON. Pay via x402 exact, $0.002 USDC on Base. Output: body.ok (bool) and body.data{ lei, valid (bool), lou_prefix, entity_part, check_digits, source }; on a malformed LEI, body.data.valid is false with a failure reason. Filters typos before a GLEIF lookup (see /v1/global/lei for the live record).

entries.name: Agentstools Environmental Compliance
entries.description: US EPA facility environmental compliance and enforcement lookup from the ECHO Detailed Facility Report: supply a facility name, EPA FRS registry id, or US address/coordinates and get the current significant-violation status overall and per statute (Clean Air Act, Clean Water Act, RCRA, Safe Drinking Water Act), quarters in noncompliance, a 3-year quarterly history, and enforcement summaries (formal/informal actions, cases, penalty dollars, last-inspection dates).

queryParams.name: Company or facility name (optionally narrowed by state)
queryParams.state: 2-letter US state code (narrows a name search)
queryParams.radius: Search radius in miles for a location lookup (default 5, max 25)

inputSchema.note: Supply ONE lookup handle: registry_id, OR name (+optional state), OR address, OR lat+lon (+optional radius).

outputSchema.description: EPA ECHO facility compliance/enforcement detail. A Detailed Facility Report failure yields a null detail block plus summary.errors and summary.partial=true rather than an error.

properties.compliance: object { current_significant_violation (bool), current_violation (bool), snc_flag (bool), programs_with_snc (int), quarters_in_noncompliance (int), overall_status (string), by_statute { CAA, CWA, RCRA, SDWA }, three_year_history { quarters[]{code,label,severity}, counts{significant,violation,compliant,no_data}, quarters_reported } }
properties.enforcement: object { inspections, days_since_last_inspection, last_inspection_date, informal_actions, formal_actions, last_formal_action_date, penalty_count, total_penalties_usd, last_penalty_usd, last_penalty_date }

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/env/compliance?<lookup handle>. Supply ONE handle as query params: registry_id (EPA FRS id), OR name (+optional state), OR address, OR lat+lon (+optional radius). No request body. Result is inline in the 200.
